# @effected/memfs constructs

| Construct | Kind | Purpose | Reach for it when |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MemoryFileSystem` | Class | An in-memory implementation of core Effect's `FileSystem` service: an isolated virtual POSIX volume — files, directories, symlinks, hard links, open descriptors, temporary resources, globbing, watching — behind the standard `FileSystem.FileSystem` key. | in-memory filesystem test double for FileSystem, seed files, inject faults, inspect writes |
| `MemoryFileSystemFaultHandler` | TypeAlias | A fault handler for one `FileSystem` method. It receives the real call arguments (path, mode, options…), so a fault can be path- or mode-specific. Returning a value replaces the call — typically `Effect.fail(PlatformError.systemError({...}))`, a `Stream`/`Sink` for the `stream`/`sink`/`watch` members, though a canned success is equally valid; returning `undefined` **declines**, delegating the call to the wrapped filesystem. The return type is the method's own, so an injected failure is constrained to the method's `PlatformError` channel — a bare `new Error` does not typecheck. This delegate-by-default posture is the whole difference from `FileSystem.layerNoop`, which denies unlisted methods. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemFaultMethod` | TypeAlias | The members of `FileSystem.FileSystem` that a fault handler can intercept: every function-valued method, the `Stream`/`Sink`-returning trio (`stream`, `sink`, `watch`) included. Only `MemoryFileSystem.failTimes` is narrower — a transient fault substitutes a failing `Effect`, so it slots into the `Effect`-returning methods alone. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemFaults` | TypeAlias | The fault registration map for `MemoryFileSystem.makeFaulty` and `MemoryFileSystem.layerFaulty`: per intercepted method, either a `MemoryFileSystemFaultHandler` or — on the `Effect`-returning methods — a `MemoryFileSystemTransientFault`. Methods absent from the map are never intercepted. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemInspectable` | Interface | The `FileSystem` service and the `MemoryFileSystemVolume` inspecting the same underlying volume — the value-level pair returned by `MemoryFileSystem.makeInspectable` and `MemoryFileSystem.makeInspectableWith`. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeed` | Interface | A volume seed: absolute POSIX paths mapped to seed entries. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeedDirectory` | Interface | A seed entry describing a directory — built with `MemoryFileSystem.directory`. The only way a seed can express an *empty* directory, and the way a directory receives an initial permission mode. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeedEntry` | TypeAlias | One value in a `MemoryFileSystemSeed`: plain file contents (`string \| Uint8Array`, unchanged from the original seed shape), or a tagged entry describing a file with a mode, a directory, or a symbolic link. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeedFile` | Interface | A seed entry describing a file, optionally carrying its initial permission mode — built with `MemoryFileSystem.file`. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSeedSymlink` | Interface | A seed entry describing a symbolic link — built with `MemoryFileSystem.symlink`. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemSyncFileSystem` | Interface | The four synchronous file operations a consumer-supplied filesystem port needs, as `MemoryFileSystem.syncFileSystem` exposes them over a volume. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemTransientFault` | Interface | A transient fault built with `MemoryFileSystem.failTimes`: usable anywhere a fault handler is, it fails a fixed number of calls with a given `PlatformError` and then delegates forever after. | |
| `MemoryFileSystemVolume` | Interface | Synchronous, read-only inspection of one memory volume — the write-path counterpart to seeding, for asserting on what a program actually wrote without routing every assertion through an `Effect` read. | |
